rows.28:f7c0:
"...I see. All right."
Mr. Kuroki nodded.
"In that case, you two can head home from here.
I'm going to give it a try myself."
"Are you serious?"
{f:I|I} asked, startled.
His face serious, Mr. Kuroki shook his head.{p}
rows.28:f898:
"Of course I am. It's something I've always wanted to know."
Then he flashed me a grin.
"But keep it a secret from everyone else.
I'll keep quiet about you two, too."
{f:I|I} nearly laughed.
Mr. Kuroki wasn't like a teacher at all.
It'd be great to get someone like him as my homeroom teacher in second year.
Thinking that, {f:I|I} answered.{p}
rows.28:f9fc: ...With Mr. Kuroki seeing us off, {f:we|we} walked out through the school gate.{p}
rows.28:fa48:
By the time I got home, my family had long since finished dinner.
Getting scolded all the while, {f:I|I} wolfed down my meal and dove into my room.
I flopped onto my bed and tried to go back over everything that had happened today.
So much really had happened{f:...|...}{p}
rows.28:fb50: Just then, the phone suddenly rang.{p}
rows.28:fb80:
Come on, now.
Didn't I tell you it was students who died here?
There's no way the ghost of some soldier with no connection to it at all would show up.
The story I heard was that if you put your ear to the wall, you could hear voices groaning in pain.{p}
rows.28:fc7c:
But think about it.
Doesn't something seem off?
The one who killed himself was supposed to be a boy, so why would a soldier's ghost show up?
Sure, there must have been soldiers among the victims brought in here.
But it just doesn't fit together, does it?
That alone makes it sound like a pretty phony story.
But I saw it the other way around: that was what made me suspicious.
If it were made up, you could just patch the details together any way you liked.{p}
rows.28:fde8: So if the story came out this half-baked, wasn't it because there was some truth in it somewhere? That's how I figured it.{p}
rows.28:fe44:
So I decided to look into it.
First, I decided to see for myself whether a ghost really appeared.
I hid in the shadows.
And I kept a secret watch on this wall.
And then, it showed up.{p}
rows.28:fef4:
A man in a military uniform rose up out of nowhere, glowing faintly.
I let out a scream.
The man turned around.
I still remember the look on his face that moment.
It was terrifying, believe me.{p}
rows.28:ffa4: He had a face like this...{p}
rows.28:ffc4:
...No, it was worse than this.
In reality, it was even scarier.{p}
rows.28:1001c:
After all, the thing wasn't human.
The man glared at me with horrible eyes.
The pressure coming off him was overwhelming.
I thought he might glare me to death.
I stood there, unable to move, and he spoke to me.
"Whoever has seen my form... I will kill..."
That's what he said.
I went white as a sheet.
To think a tiny bit of curiosity could bring on something like this...{p}
rows.28:10154: Just then, something stirred in the darkness.{p}
rows.28:101b0:
"Waaah★"
Letting out a pathetic cry, Hosoda clung to {f:me|me}.{p}
rows.28:10284:
It was a man in a plain suit{f:|}.
He gave a quick little bow, and his glasses caught the light.{p}
rows.28:102fc:
"Geez. You really scared me."
Hosoda said resentfully.
But {f:I|I} was more curious about the rest of the story.
"Mr. Kuroki... but you weren't killed, were you?
I mean, you're right here talking with {f:us|us}."{p}
rows.28:103e4:
Mr. Kuroki nodded.
"That's right. But let's take things in order."{p}
rows.28:10430:
When I saw him, it hit me what he really was.
This wasn't a ghost.
And of course it wasn't human, either.
It was the Grim Reaper... that's what I thought.
If so, it was no wonder he'd be in a place where so many people had died.
But then, did that mean he really was going to kill me?
As I started to tremble, he gave me a strange smile.
And then he opened his mouth again.
"I shall give you one chance... In X years, bring me a soul to take the place of yours.
If you cannot..."
The Reaper fell silent, but I understood.
If I didn't bring one, he'd come back and take my soul instead... that had to be what he meant.
So I answered desperately.
"All right. I'll bring you one, I swear."{p}
rows.28:10698:
...What else could I do?
I was still just a high school student.
There were so many things I wanted to do.
It was way too early for me to die.
And so I made a contract with the Reaper.{p}
rows.28:10734:
Having said that much, Mr. Kuroki looked at the man he'd called his friend.
They exchanged a meaningful smile.
I had a bad feeling about this{f:|}.
"Um... Mr. Kuroki, so..."
"Those X years are up this year."
Mr. Kuroki was smiling happily.
Then he said to the man,
"As promised, I've brought you souls.
With these, please spare me."{p}
rows.28:1086c:
Without a change in his expression, the man nodded in silence.
{f:We|We} looked back and forth between the two of them, dumbfounded.
"So you're not wearing the military uniform anymore."
That casual remark froze {f:me|me} to the spot.
This man is the Reaper{f:|}★
And if this is the year of the contract with the Reaper, that means...{p}
rows.28:10978:
"Mr. Kuroki! You mean you're giving our souls to that thing★"
Hosoda screamed it before {f:I|I} could.{p}
rows.28:109ec:
"That's right.
There's still plenty I want to do with my life."
Mr. Kuroki was grinning slyly.
"No way☆"
"Shut up! Now, go right ahead."
At his urging, the man came toward us.{p}
rows.28:10b30:
But before he could lay a single finger on him, Hosoda was sent flying{f:|}.
His huge body slammed into the wall.
The knife bounced and landed at {f:my|my} feet.
The man reached out toward Hosoda.{p}What should I do?
rows.28:10c04:
{f:I|I} decided to wait and see.
The man held his hand over Hosoda's chest.
The instant he did, Hosoda's whole body jolted and jumped.
His eyes rolled back, and he crumpled to the floor.
His arms and legs lay limply flung out, just like a stuffed doll's.
Or like clothes someone had taken off and tossed aside.
"H-Hosoda..."
{f:I|I} whispered.
Hosoda didn't move.
Was he dead{f:|}?
Had this man... no, this Reaper sucked the life right out of him{f:?|...?}
{f:I|I} panicked and tried to make a run for it.{p}
rows.28:10e68:
"Too bad. You're going to die too."
The man reached out for me.
I never should have planned that seven wonders feature.
{f:So|So} the darkness of this school ran far deeper than {f:I|I} had ever imagined.
To think that even {f:I|I} would lose my life like this.
The moment I blacked out, I heard Mr. Kuroki's voice.
"Learn all seven wonders, and something bad happens to you..."{p}
rows.28:110e0:
The knife was buried in his chest, staining it bright red.
"No... this can't be...!"
Spewing blood, he slowly collapsed to the floor.
The man... no, the Reaper held his hand over him.
A ball of light floated softly up and was drawn into the Reaper's hand.
Was that Mr. Kuroki's soul?{p}
rows.28:111ec:
The Reaper looked at {f:us|us}.
"The contract has been fulfilled..."
And then he faded from sight.
As if his body had turned to smoke.{p}
rows.28:11314:
"Don't touch me, murderer☆"
"Hosoda★"
Hosoda was shaking all over.
He'd come this close to dying, so it was only natural{f:|}.
But for him to call {f:me|me} a murderer...
If Mr. Kuroki hadn't died, {f:we|we} would both have been made sacrifices to the Reaper.
"Please calm down, Hosoda..."
When {f:I|I} moved closer, Hosoda swung his thick arms around wildly.
"D-Don't come near me! Murderer☆
Somebody help meee☆"
As if in answer to his scream, a light shone in from the far end of the hallway.{p}
rows.28:114f4: Someone was running this way with a flashlight{f:|}.{p}
rows.28:11538:
"Who's there? This area's off-limits★"
A voice I recognized.
It had to be a teacher{f:|}.
Come to think of it, it was too convenient that the day of the contract just happened to be Mr. Kuroki's night on duty.
Mr. Kuroki must have come to the old school building on his own{f:|}.
And then he'd found {f:us|us}{f:|}.
The one running toward us now was the real teacher on night duty{f:|}.
Hosoda was waving happily.
"Sir! Sir!
Help me, there's a murderer☆"
{f:I|I} looked at Mr. Kuroki's body lying there.
At the box cutter still stuck in his chest.
And at my own blood-soaked hands.
Murderer...
That's right, {f:I|I}'m a murderer{f:|}.
No matter how much I explain, nobody is ever going to understand what happened here.
{f:I|I}'m a killer who snuck into the off-limits old school building and attacked a teacher{f:|}.{p}
rows.28:11838: The flashlight beam shining on {f:me|me} was like a bug net swooping down to catch {f:me|me}.{p}
rows.28:1189c:
Hey, you got it right.
That's right.
There was a rumor that a soldier's ghost would stand in front of the wall.
But if anyone was going to haunt the place out of a grudge, wouldn't it be the boy who suffered so much?
I found that strange, so I looked into it.
And then I saw it.{p}
rows.28:11988:
The ghost of a soldier, standing there looking sad.
He was muttering something under his breath, as I recall.
I was reckless back then, so I went closer to try to make out what he was saying.
"The wall... the wall..."
That's what he kept repeating.
Then, after a while, he just vanished.{p}
rows.28:11a74:
After that, I never saw that ghost again.
And then I graduated, too.{p}
rows.28:11adc:
When I came back to this school as a teacher, I asked around, but the rumor of the soldier's ghost was gone.
Maybe even ghosts move house sometimes, huh.{p}
rows.28:11be4:
...Actually, I've seen it myself.
All kinds of faces, adults and children, rising up out of every part of this wall.
Oh, I can't forget that.
I'll probably never forget it as long as I live.
I keep telling you, there are lots of stories like this inside the old school building.
So don't go wandering in here carelessly.
You understand me?
"...Yes."
All I could do was nod.{p}
rows.28:11d38:
Mr. Kuroki smiled, satisfied.
"Good, then. Now off you go home."{p}
rows.28:11e20:
That's right.
My homeroom teacher asked me to come along and help fetch some teaching materials.{p}
rows.28:11e80:
I had a bad feeling about it, and sure enough, my teacher went to take that very route.
I was scared.
But I couldn't tell anyone why.
A high schooler can't exactly admit he's scared of ghosts, can he?
I put up with it and kept walking, but a few meters short of the ghost wall, I finally fainted.{p}
rows.28:11f88: But while I was unconscious, I had a strange experience.{p}
rows.28:11fc0: I was standing in pitch darkness.{p}
rows.28:11ff8:
When I strained my eyes, I could tell someone was there in the darkness.
And when I looked closer, see, they were corpses rotted to mush.
There were soldiers and students, children and old people.
They were all looking at me.
And they reached out their hands to me.
As if they believed I would save them.
Their fingers, skin peeled off and flesh melted down to bare bone, touched me.
Then smoke hissed up, and my body began to melt away from that spot.
They groped at me everywhere, arms, legs, all over.
And every time they did, my body crumbled away into sludge.
It was a strange feeling, hot and cold at the same time.{p}
rows.28:1220c:
When I came to, I was lying in the nurse's office.
They told me it was probably anemia.
So I figured that was why I'd had a nightmare.
But I was wrong.
On my arms and legs were the clear marks of their fingers.
I don't know what they wanted me to do for them.
But when I remember the sad looks on their faces, my heart still aches, even now.{p}
rows.28:123e0:
"Why... why..."
That's what they were saying.{p}
rows.28:12418:
"Why... why..."
For a moment, I thought I was hearing things.
In time with Mr. Kuroki's voice, a thin voice came from the wall.
A chill ran down my spine.
I could really hear a voice!{p}
rows.28:124c4:
As {f:we|we} watched, a face slowly rose up out of the wall.
A pure white face, standing out like a carving.
"Why... why..."
It kept on murmuring sadly.
Hosoda, as if drawn in by it, staggered toward the face.
"Hey, you..."
The instant he spoke to it, the face in the wall flew its eyes wide open.{p}
rows.28:127e8:
"Look☆"
I realized the whole area around us was a sea of fire.
The walls had crumbled, the pillars had snapped, and the building was in ruins{f:|}.
Just then, I heard the roar of airplanes overhead.
No way★
Mr. Kuroki put {f:my|my} fear into words.
"This is the school during the war☆"{p}
rows.28:128dc:
So it's true{f:|}★
Had the face in the wall done something{f:?|?}
But how, exactly?
No, this was no time to be thinking about that{f:|}.
I had to get out of here as fast as I {f:could|could}.
Just as I started to run, someone grabbed {f:my|my} leg.
It was Hosoda, charred black{f:|}.{p}
rows.28:12a24:
He was looking up at {f:me|me}, his skin peeled back to show the raw layer beneath.
"Don't leave me behind..."
His voice was so hoarse I could hardly believe it was the same person.
But I could tell just by looking that he couldn't be saved anymore.
{f:I|I} shook off Hosoda's arm.
"{a}{f:|}!"
A surprised, anguished voice.{p}
rows.28:12b44:
{f:I|I} covered my ears and searched for a way out.
Beyond a burning pillar, Mr. Kuroki was calling to {f:me|me}.
"Over here!"
{f:I|I} ran toward him without hesitating.
Just a little more, and I'd reach the hand he was holding out.
Twenty more centimeters.
Ten more centimeters.
And just as I thought I'd finally reach it, the ceiling came crashing down on {f:me|me}.
I leapt back on reflex.
I managed to dodge it, but the way was blocked.
"You can't escape anymore. You're going to die too."
The face in the wall said it coldly.
"Just like we did."
At my feet, I heard a low laugh.{p}
rows.28:12d4c:
"I'm so glad... that you stayed behind..."
Hosoda was grinning, and his eyes were no longer sane.{p}
rows.28:12dac:
The rubble came crashing down with a rumble.
Showers of sparks swirled up and stung my face.
{f:I|I}'m going to die here{f:|}.
In the school on the day of that air raid Mr. Kuroki told us about.
A few more corpses here wouldn't bother anyone{f:|}.
I even doubted Mr. Kuroki had made it out safely{f:|}.
But... why {f:me|me}★
Nothing answered.
{f:I|I} slowly fell, and let the flames wrap around my body.{p}
rows.28:12f50:
Ha ha ha, you're kidding, right?
After all the scares I'd had, would I really make a bet like that with a friend?
It was a situation I just couldn't get out of.
What was it, you ask?{p}
rows.28:12ff0: Actually, it was an evacuation drill.{p}
rows.28:1300c:
Looking back now, it was a stupid thing to do.
At first, it was just a little argument.
My friend and I got to arguing about which of us was faster.
So we decided to have a race.{p}
rows.28:130cc:
Only, it was a rainy day.
So we decided to race inside the school building.
Of course, we'd get chewed out if a teacher found out, so we did it on the sly after school.
And the course went right past that wall.
I thought, this is bad.
But if I complained, they'd say I'd chickened out.
And of course, there was absolutely no backing out at that point.
So I had no choice but to face the wall I hated so much.
At our buddy's signal, we shot off and rounded the corner almost neck and neck.
No, maybe I was a little in the lead.
And then we ran past the wall.
Suddenly, it felt like someone had grabbed my shoulder.
I turned around, and a girl was standing there.
Yes, she was wearing a sailor uniform, so I think she was probably a girl.
Why do I put it like that, you ask?
Because there was nothing above the sailor uniform.
Where her head should have been, there was just a gaping empty space.
"I've lost my head."
That's what she said.
"So give me yours."
Just like that.
And then I noticed I was surrounded by ghosts, lots of them.{p}
